characterizations.result_summary: Confirmed monosubstitution pattern of PSBPhBr, high degree of functionalization of quinolate polymers, tetracoordinated boron centers, and functionalization degree of copolymer PSBPhQ-H-co-PSSiMe<sub>3</sub>.

parameters.detectors: refractive index (RI) and multiangle laser light scattering (MALLS)

characterizations.result_summary: Monomodal elution profiles with narrow PDI (1.11-1.18) observed for all polymers; absolute molecular weights determined, DP nearly unchanged relative to starting PSSiMe<sub>3</sub>, no backbone cleavage or cross-linking during synthesis.
Glass transition temperatures of quinolate polymers range from 210 to 275 °C.
Decomposition temperatures over 300 °C; up to 30% residual material observed after heating to 800 °C under nitrogen.

In contrast, when we monitored the <sup>1</sup>H NMR spectra of the tert-butylphenyl-substituted quinolate polymers both in wet and oxygenated solvents and as solids in air, no sign of decomposition was found for at least 4 weeks, and the GPC traces were virtually identical to those of the freshly prepared polymer samples.

Thus, the stability of the quinolate polymers with phenyl groups on boron is significantly improved relative to those containing electron-rich thiophene groups, and the polymers can easily be handled under ambient conditions for extended periods of time.
